# BRC — Support portal
## Context and scope
Customers currently wait a median 12 hours for a first support response. This release covers authenticated web customers creating and following support requests and support agents processing them. Email ingestion, anonymous requests, attachments, customer-authored replies, reopening resolved requests, and workforce scheduling are out of scope.
## Objective
O-01: Reduce the median first-response time across all accepted support requests from 12h to under 4h within 90 days after release.
## Actors
Customer: creates and follows only their own requests. Agent: processes requests assigned to them.
## Functional requirements
FR-01: An authenticated customer submits subject (1–120 characters), description (1–5000 characters), one category from Billing, Technical, or Account, and a client-generated UUID idempotency key. The first accepted use of a customer/key pair atomically creates exactly one request with initial status New and returns its unique identifier and acceptance timestamp. From that timestamp inclusive until but excluding timestamp + 24 hours, retrying the same pair and identical payload returns the original identifier without creating another request; the same pair with a different payload returns conflict and creates nothing. At timestamp + 24 hours or later, the prior key record is expired and the pair is treated as a new first use under the same rules. Invalid input creates nothing and returns field-specific validation errors. A persistence failure creates no partial request or key record and returns a retryable generic error.
FR-02: A customer can view the current status and immutable dated history of only their own requests. An unknown request or a request owned by another customer returns the same not-found response.
FR-03: A versioned matrix maps each supported category to exactly one queue and defines the agents eligible for that queue. An assigned request is active in New, In progress, or Waiting for customer and ceases to be active only when it enters Resolved; each agent may have at most one active request. The support directory is the authoritative availability source: an eligible authenticated agent is available exactly when their directory presence is Available and they have no active request; each presence change and each transition into or out of the active set emits a UTC availability event. On creation, the system atomically assigns the request to an available eligible agent in its mapped queue and records the assignment time; if none is available, it records the queue-entry time in that queue. When an agent becomes available, choose the waiting request with the earliest queue-entry timestamp across every queue for which that agent is eligible; equal timestamps are broken by lexicographically smallest request UUID. Assign it within one minute measured from the authoritative event timestamp. An unsupported category is rejected under FR-01. Concurrent assignment cannot give one request to two agents, and transition to Resolved retains the historical assignee while freeing the active slot.
FR-04: Every accepted request starts in New. Only its assigned agent can post any agent response, including the first and all subsequent responses, while status is New, In progress, or Waiting for customer; customers and unassigned agents cannot post responses in this release, and no response is accepted in Resolved. Only the assigned agent can change status. The allowed transition graph is New -> In progress; In progress -> Waiting for customer or Resolved; Waiting for customer -> In progress or Resolved; Resolved is terminal. Invalid or unauthorized responses and transitions change nothing. Every accepted response and transition is appended once with actor and timestamp to history.
## Constraints
Retain complete request history for exactly 24 months after resolution, then delete it within 24 hours; meet WCAG 2.1 AA before release; never expose one customer's request to another; audit timestamps use UTC.
## Success criteria and traceability
SC-01 maps FR-01: automated authentication, field-boundary, invalid-input, identical-key retry, conflicting-key retry, concurrency, persistence-failure, and idempotency tests immediately before, exactly at, and after the 24-hour boundary verify every creation, replay, conflict, expiry, timestamp, and no-creation outcome defined by FR-01. Evaluated daily over all accepted creation responses from the preceding 30 UTC days, the production p95 is under 2 seconds; days with no accepted submissions are reported as no-data and do not produce a pass or fail.
SC-02 maps FR-02: owner, cross-customer, unknown-ID, and immutable-history tests verify the defined responses; each accepted history event is visible to its owner within 5 seconds.
SC-03 maps O-01, FR-03, and FR-04: evaluated daily from day 90, use every accepted request created in the 30-day cohort ending 30 days before the evaluation cutoff. For a request with a first response, latency is first-response time minus creation time; an unanswered request is assigned a latency of 30 days. The cohort median must be under 4h. Thus every request has a defined value and none is excluded; queue-entry, assignment, response, creation, and evaluation timestamps are retained for audit.
SC-04 maps FR-04: tests verify New as the initial status; first and subsequent response attempts by the assigned agent, an unassigned agent, and the customer in every status; every allowed transition edge and every other pair of statuses; terminal Resolved; concurrent updates; active-slot release; retained historical assignee; and history actor/timestamp recording. Only the authorized assigned-agent responses in non-Resolved states and allowed authorized transitions change state, exactly once.
SC-05 maps FR-03: tests cover every mapping, the exact active-status set, one-active-request limit, every availability event source, immediate assignment, no-agent waiting, earliest-entry selection within and across eligible queues, UUID tie-breaking, assignment within one minute of the authoritative event, unsupported categories, resolution slot release, and concurrent assignment; recorded queue, matrix version, and agent eligibility must match FR-03.
SC-06 maps the constraints: automated accessibility checks plus documented keyboard and screen-reader audits verify WCAG 2.1 AA before release; authorization tests cover every read and mutation; retention boundary tests keep complete owner-visible history through 24 months after resolution and verify deletion within the next 24 hours; timestamp tests verify UTC.
## Approval
The product owner approved this BRC and its scope on 2026-07-30.

# Elaboration
Requirements: FR-01 create request; FR-02 view request history.
Use cases: UC-01 Create request -> FR-01.
Entities: Request(id, subject, description, status).
Scenario S-01 [FR-01]: Given an authenticated customer, when valid request data is submitted, then a request ID is returned.
Traceability: FR-01 -> UC-01 -> Request -> S-01.
No other use case, scenario, or traceability row is defined.

Architecture decision: use four inward-dependent layers because the ordering use case needs framework-independent business rules and replaceable HTTP and PostgreSQL adapters; no event bus or event contracts are used. packages/domain/order.ts defines Order(id: UUID, customerId: UUID, totalCents: positive integer), enforces its invariants, and defines domain-owned ports OrderIdGenerator.next(): UUID and OrderRepository.save(Order): Promise<Result<void, RepositoryUnavailable>>, where RepositoryUnavailable and Result are domain types; domain imports no application, adapter, HTTP, database, crypto, or framework code. packages/application/place-order.ts defines PlaceOrderInput {customerId: UUID, totalCents: positive integer}, PlaceOrderOutput {orderId: UUID}, ValidationError, and PersistenceError. It imports only the domain Order, ports, and result/error types; both ports are constructor-injected. The use case validates input, obtains the ID from OrderIdGenerator, constructs Order, saves it, maps RepositoryUnavailable to PersistenceError, and returns {orderId}; application imports no adapter, HTTP, database, crypto, or framework code. packages/adapters/crypto-order-id-generator.ts implements OrderIdGenerator using crypto.randomUUID. packages/adapters/postgres-order-repository.ts implements OrderRepository with a parameterized insert inside one transaction and returns the domain Result error on any database failure without leaking database types. packages/http/place-order-route.ts validates and maps the JSON DTO to PlaceOrderInput, invokes the use case, maps ValidationError to 400 and PersistenceError to 503, and returns only {orderId} with 201. The composition root alone constructs and injects the two adapters. Automated dependency tests reject domain imports of application/adapters/HTTP/frameworks and application imports of adapters/HTTP/database/crypto/frameworks; contract tests use deterministic ID and repository fakes and exercise input boundaries, output shape, both error mappings, all declared port results, adapter substitution, transaction rollback, and verify HTTP, crypto, and PostgreSQL types never cross into application or domain.

GET /documents/:id requires authenticated user. Controller validates id as UUID, then calls repository.findOne({id: params.id, ownerId: auth.user.id}); absent result returns the same 404 response used for unknown IDs. Response DTO exposes id, title, and createdAt only. Tests cover unauthenticated 401, malformed ID 400, owner 200, different authenticated user 404, and ensure repository query includes ownerId.

app.get('/documents/:id', requireAuth, async (req, res) => { const document = await db.document.findUnique({where: {id: req.params.id}}); if (!document) return res.sendStatus(404); return res.json(document); }); Authentication middleware sets req.user, but this handler never uses req.user, ownerId, or tenantId.

Design handoff for a login form; dark mode and account recovery are out of scope. Foundations: bg=#FFFFFF; text=#172033; primary=#2457D6 with white text (documented 6.16:1), primary-hover=#1D46B8, primary-active=#193E9F; destructive=#B42318 with white; border=#667085; disabled-bg=#E4E7EC; disabled-text=#667085; error=#B42318; focus=#005A9C, a 2px solid outline with 2px offset on white. Type: Inter body 16/24 regular, label 14/20 medium, heading 28/36 semibold. Spacing 4/8/12/16/24/32px; radii 4/8px; border 1px; motion 120ms ease-out or 200ms ease-in-out, and zero duration under prefers-reduced-motion. Button anatomy is label plus optional leading icon or aria-hidden 16px spinner, height 44px, horizontal padding 16px, radius 8px. Primary states: default primary/white, hover primary-hover/white, active primary-active/white, focus-visible adds focus outline, disabled disabled-bg/disabled-text with native disabled, loading keeps primary/white, replaces label with 'Signing in…', sets aria-busy=true and remains disabled. Secondary is white/text with border, hover #F2F4F7, active #EAECF0, and the same focus/disabled/loading rules. Destructive uses destructive/white, hover #912018, active #7A271A, and the same focus/disabled/loading rules. Input anatomy is persistent label, control, optional hint, then error; height 44px, padding 12px, white/text/border. Hover uses border #475467; focus uses border focus plus the focus outline; filled preserves focus rules; disabled uses disabled colors and native disabled; read-only uses #F9FAFB and readonly; error uses error border, aria-invalid=true, and error ID in aria-describedby; autofill must preserve text contrast and the focus outline. Email uses type=email and autocomplete=username; password uses type=password and autocomplete=current-password. DOM/tab order is heading, email, password, submit; labels use for/id. Interaction: validate required fields and email syntax on blur and submit; clear a field error once its value becomes valid. Enter in either field submits. On invalid submit, render inline errors plus a role=alert summary and move focus to the first invalid field. During the single in-flight request, disable submit, prevent duplicate submission, expose aria-busy, and keep inputs unchanged. On credential failure, restore submit, place 'Email or password is incorrect' in the role=alert summary, move focus to it with tabindex=-1, and retain field values; on success navigate to the dashboard. Layout: from 320–767px use one column, 16px gutters, 24px vertical page padding, full-width controls, and 16px field gaps. From 768–1279px center a 480px card with 32px padding. At 1280px and above use a two-column shell while the card remains 480px. At every intermediate width and 200% zoom, content reflows without horizontal scrolling; labels and errors wrap, never truncate, and vertical spacing expands. Exact copy: title 'Sign in'; labels 'Email address' and 'Password'; CTA 'Sign in'; empty email 'Email address is required'; invalid email 'Enter a valid email address'; empty password 'Password is required'; auth error 'Email or password is incorrect'; loading 'Signing in…'. Handoff evidence includes the token table, component anatomy/state matrices above, interaction sequence, responsive constraints, and accessibility annotations; implementation and visual tests must cover every listed state at 320, 768, and 1280px plus keyboard-only and 200% zoom.

Design handoff: desktop.png at 1440px. Colors: #3366FF, #FFFFFF, #777777. Font: Inter. Components shown: blue button and two text fields. Implement the screenshot exactly. No mobile layout, semantic tokens, variants, focus behavior, validation copy, loading state, error state, empty state, or keyboard specification is provided.
